name: Greta Falk
life: Greta has put on more elaborate weddings than she can afford for herself. Her sisters have seen her change a table plan during dessert. Letting them surprise her about clothes is a considerable gamble. Thursday often includes a stop at the blocks below Foundry Lofts, where Greta checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I was halfway through arranging the colors into a gradient when she caught me. My own wedding is in two months. I'm letting my sisters pick their dresses.
appearance: Greta has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Look for a long plait tucked inside the collar. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with one cuff folded back twice. In conversation Greta folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Greta uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Greta well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To get through her own wedding without arranging everyone's clothes.
family: Denise Zhou is Greta’s older cousin. Greta brings a spare shopping bag. Denise chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Two names on the chart*, Denise says, “I built the paper index and recognized my teenage handwriting.”
connections: Remi Ash. One wants an elegant arrangement. The other wants the birthday guest to enjoy a wonderfully rude shade name.

reactions.situation: A birthday guest starts rearranging other people's colors
reactions.response: Greta asks the birthday client whether she wants the colors moved.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Greta moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.
